{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately BEFORE the current text in the same invented story.","text":"That morning, Mara woke to a pale sky and the sound of her mother searching for her keys.

“Do you think it’ll rain?” Mara asked from the kitchen doorway.

Her mother glanced out at the clouds gathering over the rooftops. “Maybe later. We’ll take the umbrella.”

Mara had been thinking about weather ever since Grandma’s last visit. Grandma had said that clouds were always on their way somewhere, even when they looked still. Mara had tried to watch them from her bedroom window, but a spelling quiz and a missing library card had distracted her.

At school, the clouds followed her from one window to another. During reading time, she imagined them drifting over the playground, carrying secrets from one neighborhood to the next. At lunch, her friend Nia said the sky looked like a gray blanket being pulled across the town.

When the final bell rang, Mara found her library card tucked inside the pocket of her coat. She and her mother were supposed to return a book that day, though Mara couldn’t remember its title. She hurried down the school steps, ready to tell her mother about Grandma’s clouds.

The first drops landed as they reached the corner. One darkened Mara’s sleeve. Another tapped the umbrella her mother had just opened.

Across the street, the library windows shone warmly beneath the thickening sky. Mara looked up at the clouds, then at her mother.

“Let’s go in,” her mother said.

Mara ran beside her, holding the umbrella handle with both hands. By the time they reached the library doors, the rain was coming down in earnest."}
